name: Raema
title: Son of Cush
summary: Raema (also spelled Raama) was a son of Cush and grandson of Ham, Noah's son. He is mentioned in the genealogy of Genesis as part of the origins of nations after the flood. His descendants are counted among the peoples who settled in the Arabian Peninsula.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Table of Nations
keyEvents.description: Raema is listed as one of the sons of Cush in the genealogy of nations after the flood in Genesis.

keyEvents.title: Raema's Descendants
keyEvents.description: Raema's sons Sheba and Dedan are mentioned as founders of peoples on the Arabian Peninsula.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Raema's lineage is repeated in 1 Chronicles as part of the expanded genealogical history from Adam onward.

keyEvents.title: Cush's Descendants and Their Dispersion
keyEvents.description: As part of Ham's lineage, Raema's descendants spread out and formed their own ethnic groups in accordance with God's plan to fill the earth after the flood.

keyEvents.title: Connection to Trading Peoples
keyEvents.description: Raema's descendants, especially Sheba and Dedan, later became known as traders and are mentioned in prophetic writings as important trading partners.
